name: Nyuta (Anna) Federmesser / VERA Hospice Charity Foundation / Lighthouse children's hospice (with predecessor Vera Millionschikova / First Moscow Hospice)
location: Moscow and ~60 regions of Russia; First Moscow Hospice 1994; Lighthouse children's hospice opened October 2019

The office is morphine, prescription, refill, and the refusal to let a dying person be punished for the state's drug-policy anxiety.

evidence: Wikipedia Anna Federmesser; SPID.center 2018 English interview; Vice/Coda 2024 long-form; ehospice government action plan; BEARR Trust

name: Isshinji temple (one-spirit-per-urn / Okotsubutsu practice) and Ending Center NPO (grave-friends model) - Japanese muenbotoke offices
location: Isshinji - Tennoji ward, Osaka, Japan (practice from 1887, ~decadal); Ending Center - Tokyo periphery, founded by sociologist Inoue Haruyo
office: Disconnected-dead-no-kin / muenbotoke / interment without a legal successor
status: OFFICE-CANON; INSTITUTION-CANDIDATES, NOT SINGLE-FOUNDER CANON
work: Isshinji combines cremated remains donated to the temple into a Buddha statue (Okotsubutsu) roughly once per decade, regardless of prior religious affiliation, at modest Japanese-funeral-standards fees (¥20,000-¥50,000). Ending Center is an NPO with members who pay a one-time fee, attend workshops and 'grave-friend' (haka tomo) meetings, and are interred together rather than with biological kin.
why: Japanese law and conventional Buddhist parish practice require a legal successor to maintain a family grave through ongoing fees; a person without successor becomes muenbotoke (buddha without bonds). Wealthy-aging-society counterpart to the migrant-grave office and to the cube's homeless-memorial office.
flags: Buddhist temples have a structural revenue interest in graves (the danka system); these models are partly reform of that system, not pure mercy; cherry-tree aesthetics should not substitute for analysis; the kodokushi private cleaning industry is paid commercial service rather than the costly mercy the cube studies, though workers describe the work in language much closer to mercy than to industry copy.
evidence: SSRC Immanent Frame Anne Allison 2021; Uncanny Japan podcast; Project MUSE review of Mark Rowe Bonds of the Dead; Nippon.com January 2026

name: Sudan Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs / غرف الطوارئ) - rooted in the nafir / nafeer tradition
location: Sudan - all 18 states; particularly Khartoum, Omdurman, Darfur, and Gezira
office: Collapsed-state-neighborhood-kitchen / civilian-led survival threshold during armed conflict and famine
status: OFFICE-CANON; NETWORK-CANDIDATE; KEEP WITH WAR-CONTEXT, DONOR-LEVERAGE, AND ANONYMITY FLAGS
work: Decentralised volunteer civilian-led mutual-aid networks emerged from the 2019 Resistance Committees, mobilised first against COVID-19, became Sudan's de facto humanitarian backbone after the April 2023 outbreak of war between SAF and RSF; over 11.5 million people assisted by late 2024; in Khartoum State alone ~162 base ERRs with 4,000+ volunteers running takaya community kitchens, neighbourhood clinics, evacuations, infrastructure repair, refuges for survivors of conflict-related rape; Women's Response Rooms adapt the traditional soondooq savings model.
why: The threshold is from neighbourhood-with-infrastructure to neighbourhood-the-war-wants-empty; the office is the kitchen that does not close, the clinic with a running generator, the WhatsApp room that arranges evacuation across active front lines. Mercy as horizontal mutual practice, not vertical rescue.
flags: Roughly 160 volunteers killed by late 2024; many detained, tortured, or disappeared; both warring sides routinely accuse ERRs of espionage; US declared ongoing genocide January 2025 - donor-comfort 'two sides equally to blame' framing must be resisted; ERRs themselves resist external recasting as a single charismatic organisation; cube should preserve their decentralised anonymity-protective character; international recognition (Nobel Peace Prize nomination 2025; Right Livelihood Award 2025) is now substantial - no longer unknown work but office too important to omit.
evidence: Right Livelihood laureate profile; Chatham House December 2024; The New Humanitarian 2023; Khartoum ERR self-description; Wikipedia ERRs; Mutual Aid Sudan Coalition; Upstream Journal December 2024; CMI policy brief; Giving Compass / Devex March 2026

name: Lalish rebaptism office / Yazidi Spiritual Council — Baba Sheikh Khurto Hajji Ismail (d. 2020), Khidher Domle, successor Hazim Tahsin Beg
location: Lalish temple, Sheikhan district, Duhok Governorate, Kurdistan Region of Iraq
office: Doctrinal-return-after-captivity / religious community readmission of forcibly converted and sexually enslaved survivors / anti-erasure inside the survivor's own community
status: OFFICE-CANON; INSTITUTION-CANDIDATE WITH NAMED ADVOCATES; KEEP WITH INTERNAL-LIMITS, CHILD-EXCLUSION, AND PURIFICATION-LANGUAGE FLAGS
work: September 2014 decree by Baba Sheikh declared survivors of ISIS captivity remained Yazidi and welcomed back without honour-killing or excommunication; survivors received at Lalish for rebaptism with water from the temple's holy spring; ~500 women in the first two years per Lalish elders; office continues under successor Hazim Tahsin Beg after Baba Sheikh's October 2020 death; advocate Khidher Domle (University of Dohuk) credited with brokering the doctrinal change.
why: First explicitly theological / communal-doctrinal threshold office the cube holds. Before 2014 forced conversion or rape would have meant Yazidi excommunication; the doctrinal change in the time scale of a genocide is rare. The threshold is the temple gate; the office is the rebaptism, the public welcome, the refusal to let the perpetrator's verdict become the community's.

'Purification' framing of rebaptism risks implying the woman, not the perpetrator, needed cleansing — noted without dismissing leaders' own framing. Do not name individual survivors as proof of office.

name: Débora Maria da Silva / Mães de Maio (Mothers of May) — Brazil
location: Baixada Santista and São Paulo state, Brazil; translocal voice through Conectas Direitos Humanos

status: KEEP WITH FAMILY-OF-VICTIM AND STATE-PERPETRATOR FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR THE BRAZILIAN VARIANT OF SEARCH-FOR-THE-DISAPPEARED
work: After Crimes of May 12-21 2006 (PCC attacks followed by São Paulo Military Police and extermination-group retaliation killing 500+ civilians, overwhelmingly young Black men from peripheries), Débora and other bereaved mothers founded Mães de Maio; her son Edson Rogério Silva dos Santos, a gari, was shot dead 15 May 2006 at a gas station in Baixada Santista; 20-year anniversary marked May 2026 with extensive Brazilian press coverage; one police officer imprisoned for three deaths; work with Conectas to bring case to UN.

Where Mexican searcher-mothers face a typical cartel killer plus a non-investigating state, the Brazilian case faces uniformed state agents and allied extermination squads as the direct killers; the bodies were not missing but the cause was. The office converts grief into a public record the state will not produce.

Débora is recognised (Dandara dos Palmares, Cidadã Paulistana, Medalha Chico Mendes); not unknown-canon. Cube follows network's own 'Crimes of May' framing; does not name specific victims for aesthetic effect.

name: Good Nanum (좋은 나눔) / Park Jin-ok — and Nanum and Nanum (나눔과 나눔) — South Korea
location: Goyang, Seoul, and other South Korean cities; Nanum and Nanum operates the Seoul Public Funeral consultation hotline ([public consultation hotline number redacted — non-referral cube])

work: Good Nanum (directed by Park Jin-ok) holds one-day funerals with portrait, name tablet, Buddhist or Christian rites for people whose bodies go unclaimed at hospitals, flophouses, and police morgues; ~month-long waiting period for family to come forward; cremation and charnel-house interment. Growing state involvement raises the standard state-proximity question. name: Crystal Paikea / Te Tai Tokerau suicide postvention team — with Fusion (Te Tai Tokerau ki Muriwhenua, 2012) and Te Arawa postvention work (Tepora Emery, Candy Cookson Cox)
location: Te Tai Tokerau / Northland, Aotearoa New Zealand; population ~179,000 in the Tai Tokerau team's catchment
office: Suicide-postvention threshold / whānau-grounded support for those bereaved by whakamomori (suicide) / indigenous reframing of stigma
status: KEEP; OFFICE-CANON FOR INDIGENOUS-LED SUICIDE POSTVENTION; TEAM-CANDIDATE WITH NAMED LEAD
work: Health New Zealand Te Whatu Ora team of three led by Crystal Paikea providing face-to-face postvention support across Te Tai Tokerau using tangi practice, whānau visits as manuhiri, kaupapa Māori method; explicitly non-clinical; works with families for years. Fusion interagency group established 2012 after 19 youth deaths in the region. Te Arawa postvention tool developed after rangatahi suicides 2008-2012. Framework: Turamarama Declaration (2017), He Tapu te Oranga o ia Tangata 2019-2024 plan.
why: Cube's first office focused on the bereaved survivor rather than the dying or the dead. Indigenous framework recovers a pre-colonial conceptualisation of suicide as whakamomori (overwhelming sadness) and kahupō (spiritual blindness) met with aroha rather than shame — the office is not reducing stigma it inherited but recovering a frame that pre-existed colonial stigma.
flags: Operates inside state health service Te Whatu Ora — inverse of the Federmesser state-proximity question (here state agency hosts indigenous-led work; office good in spite of host, not because of it). Northland youth-suicide inquest evidence indicates clinical mental health services have repeatedly failed Māori rangatahi. Suicide is cube's most sensitive topic; candidate file avoids method, specific statistics, identifying detail.
evidence: NZ Herald November 2024 on Crystal Paikea and the inquest; HQSC Fusion case study; Te Whatu Ora He Arotake review July 2024; HRC NZ on Te Arawa postvention research; Aspin et al. Kōtuitui 2024; NZ Doctor coverage of He Arotake

status: KEEP WITH WAR-CONTEXT, BLOCKADE, AND FUNDER-DIVERSITY FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR THE YEMENI VARIANT OF COLLAPSED-STATE-NEIGHBORHOOD-KITCHEN
work: Founded 2015 by Fatik Al-Rodaini, a Sanaa-born journalist; named for the woman who made the first $1,000 donation; grew from #20ForYemen Twitter campaign ($4,200 / 150 families fed for a month) to over 7M meals distributed by 2017; all food purchased locally to circumvent blockade; team mostly Yemeni journalists/activists turned humanitarians; regular monthly food packages to Yemen's tiny remaining Jewish minority in Sanaa since 2016.
why: Yemeni parallel to Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms; civilian-led, locally-sourced, operating where international NGOs cannot reach. Adds blockade as a distinct condition from active war.
flags: Al-Rodaini's pre-2015 career included roles in former President Saleh's office of electronic media; cube notes this without judgment. Funding from highly diverse small-donor sources (Patreon, IndieGoGo, GoFundMe) due to blockade restrictions. Al-Rodaini speaks publicly about Western complicity in the war ('Saudi money talks') — cube records this as his position. Volunteers have been targeted while delivering aid. Cube does not name individual recipients as proof of office.
evidence: Mona Relief official site; Middle East Monitor interview (Aug 2020); PRX The World 2017; CARE Yemen 2020; Alistair Reign News Blog 2015; Mona Relief media archive (Jewish community deliveries since 2016)

name: Kenya Cuevas / Casa de las Muñecas Tiresias — Casa Hogar Paola Buenrostro and successor shelters — with parallel Casa Frida and Casa Arcoíris — Mexico
location: Mexico — Casa Hogar Paola Buenrostro in CDMX (Jan 2020); Casa Hogar Catherinne Danielle Márquez in Cuernavaca, Morelos (Feb 2022); Casa Hogar Kaory Catarero Regalado in Apaxco, Estado de México (2023); parallel Casa Frida (CDMX/Tapachula/Monterrey) and Casa Arcoíris (Tijuana)
office: Chosen-family-for-trans-and-queer-adults / shelter, sober living, prison reentry, legal/identity advocacy for trans women, gay men, and queer migrants
status: KEEP WITH FAMILY-OF-VICTIM, RECOGNITION, AND CULT-OF-PERSONALITY FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR CHOSEN-FAMILY-FOR-TRANS-AND-QUEER-ADULTS
work: Kenya Cuevas — trans woman, sex worker, survivor of prison, addiction, HIV diagnosis — founded the network after the 30 September 2016 murder of her friend Paola Buenrostro in CDMX's La Merced. Casa Hogar Paola Buenrostro opened January 2020 as Mexico's first dedicated shelter for trans women; network now spans three houses. Work includes prison legal-literacy workshops for trans women, post-release pickup and integration. Served ~1,800 (2018, pre-shelter) and ~10,000 (2020). Casa Frida (founded May 2020) served 423 LGBTIQ+ refugees and reintegrated 349 by early 2024.
why: rev0012 SearchTrail named trans chosen-family work without naming minors. These shelters are the right shape — adults, named at their own names, reconnected when biological families and the Mexican state have failed them.
flags: Latin America accounts for ~70% of global registered trans murders. Cuevas has received significant international recognition (2022 Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights Award) — public-figure visibility flag. Leadership has been described as personalistic; successor question not yet resolved. Shelters partly funded through CDMX government and corporate donations — standard state-proximity DOOR-ETHICS question. Mixed user reviews note administrative friction. Residents not named as proof of office.
evidence: Washington Blade 2021; Casa Frida website; GIRE/Karen Villalobos Feb 2024; El Diario.es Feb 2022; Homosensual Jan 2024; Agencia Presentes Dec 2021; USF Master's Thesis 2024

name: Pastor Nelson Moz / Eben-Ezer Baptist Church and Pastor Nestor Cruz / Hungry Church — El Salvador (with companion person-benchmark canon Greg Boyle / Homeboy Industries)
location: San Salvador and elsewhere in El Salvador; particularly evangelical churches in former MS-13 and Barrio 18 territories
office: Religious exit-ramp / reentry-from-gang via faith community / the rare departure from a gang the gang will permit
status: KEEP WITH STATE-OF-EMERGENCY ENDANGERMENT, EVANGELICAL-FRAMING, AND CONVERSION-AS-PRECONDITION FLAGS; OFFICE-CANON FOR THE NON-US PARALLEL TO HOMEBOY INDUSTRIES
work: In El Salvador gangs do not let members 'retire'; departure typically means death. The two near-universal exceptions are emigration and conversion to an evangelical church. Pastor Nelson Moz has led Eben-Ezer Baptist Church in San Salvador for 20+ years, surviving multiple police raids during worship under the post-2022 state of emergency. Pastor Nestor Cruz founded Hungry Church for MS-13-affiliated deportees returning to El Salvador after US prison; provides housing, microbusiness (eggs, pupusas), and from 2018 carpentry/auto-mechanics training partly funded through Salvadoran Lutheran Church/ELCA. Research by José Miguel Cruz (FIU) finds >50% of surveyed Salvadoran gang members identify as evangelical.
why: rev0012 SearchTrail named 'prison reentry beyond the US' specifically. The Salvadoran and Honduran evangelical reentry offices are the most documented non-US case of the gang/prison reentry office and the most endangered — pastors arrested under Bukele's March 2022 state of emergency.
flags: Conversion as precondition: the gang surveils former members for visible church attendance, sobriety, and avoidance of crime; will kill a member who 'fails as a Christian.' Cube notes this without endorsing evangelical-only framing. Bukele state-of-emergency arrests have undone years of pastoral reinsertion work. Some sources withhold pastors' real names; cube uses names already public and does not name individuals at risk. Greg Boyle / Homeboy Industries kept as PERSON-BENCHMARK only (too famous, US-centric).
evidence: CSM Sep 2017; CPR/NPR Jul 2018; Newsweek Sep 2019; America Magazine Apr 2022; Grand Canyon Synod ELCA on Hungry Church; Amnesty International Aug 2022; Conciliation Resources on 2012 truce; UMNews on Honduras pastoral work

name: Marius Romme, Sandra Escher, Patsy Hage / Hearing Voices Movement / Intervoice — translocal
location: Origin Maastricht, Netherlands (1987); now Intervoice and national Hearing Voices Networks in ~29 countries
office: Peer-led psychiatric crisis support / non-pathologising frame for voice-hearing / refusal of the medical model as the only model
status: OFFICE-CANON; FOUNDER-PLUS-VOICE-HEARER NETWORK CANDIDATE; KEEP WITH DECEASED-PROFESSOR, ACADEMIC-PROXIMITY, AND MEDICATION-DEBATE FLAGS
work: 1987 Dutch TV appeal by Romme (psychiatrist), Escher (journalist/child psychologist), and Hage (voice-hearer) drew hundreds of voice-hearer responses; formed the basis of the movement. Premises: voice-hearing is a meaningful human experience (~2-4% of population hears voices without psychiatric contact); voices best understood in trauma/life context; peer support is essential. UK network founded 1988 (Manchester). Intervoice incorporated as UK not-for-profit 2007, Romme president until his 2021 death. SAMHSA 'promising practice' designation. Successor leadership includes Jacqui Dillon, Eleanor Longden, Dirk Corstens, Mark Morris.
why: rev0012 SearchTrail named psychiatric peer-support. Open Dialogue (Western Lapland) is a state public-health system, wrong shape for cube. Hearing Voices Movement is the peer-led counterpart — Hearing Voices Groups in living rooms and church halls before earning their place in policy.
flags: Romme was a psychiatry professor — office not strictly 'unknown canon' though groups themselves are peer-led. Uneasy relationship with mainstream psychiatric research methods. Some clinicians remain critical; cube does not adjudicate clinical dispute. Movement does not require non-medication but has at times read as anti-medication. Individual voice-hearers not named or described as proof of office beyond their own self-chosen testimony in published research.
evidence: Tandfonline Living Tribute to Romme (2022); Schizophrenia Bulletin (Corstens et al. 2014); Hearing Voices Network UK; Intervoice; Hearing Voices Network USA; Understanding Voices; Lancet Psychiatry 2015; Wikipedia

location: Kiribati; Tarawa and Kiritimati public-office line
office: First women-and-children SGBV support centre / helpline, counselling, legal advice, case management, and crisis shelter
status: KEEP; PACIFIC SURVIVOR-CARE FIND; SMALL-ISLAND SUPPORT-CENTRE ENTRY WITH OPERATIONAL-SAFETY FLAG
work: Feminist non-profit government organisation supporting women and children survivors of sexual and gender-based violence through counselling, legal advice/support, case management, 24/7 helpline, survivor support fund, advocacy/awareness, and crisis-shelter initiative.
why: The office is the first named door in Kiribati for women and children experiencing SGBV: phone, counsellor, legal explanation, case support, and safe referral without making the survivor carry the system alone.
flags: Do not use as live referral directory; verify current capacity; no shelter logistics; government-proximate source base; protect children/survivors.
evidence: KWCSC official site; KIT/KWCSC training and MOU source; FindAHelpline KWCSC listing.

name: Kiribati SafeNet / Our Lady of the Sacred Heart crisis centre line
office: National GBV referral mesh plus long-term accommodation threshold
status: NETWORK-CANDIDATE / INSTITUTION-CANDIDATE; KEEP WITH FAITH-BASED-SHELTER AND NETWORK-CAPACITY FLAGS
work: SafeNet is a national government/NGO frontline-provider network for GBV survivors; public UN Women reporting links police reforms, temporary shelter access, survivor support fund access, and OLSH long-term accommodation for women and girls who survived violence.
why: The survivor should not have to know which office, unit, shelter, clinic, fund, or counsellor comes next. The office is routing without abandonment.
flags: Faith-based accommodation requires autonomy/precondition check; network capacity not equal to available beds/transport; avoid operational detail.
evidence: UN Micronesia / UN Women SafeNet Kiribati story, July 2025.

name: Chuuk Women’s Council / Tongen Inepwineu Counselling Centre (TICC) / APIMAR SafeNet
location: Chuuk State, Federated States of Micronesia
office: First crisis support counselling centre in FSM / safe counsellors and referral mesh
status: KEEP; NORTH-PACIFIC FIRST-CRISIS-CENTRE LINE; NETWORK-CANDIDATE WITH DONOR-AND-CAPACITY FLAGS
work: TICC provides free, confidential, non-judgmental counselling and trained safe counsellors for survivors of domestic violence, rape, sexual harassment, and child sexual abuse, connected to the APIMAR SafeNet referral system.
why: A small first door in a scattered-island setting: trained safe counsellors and a referral mesh where police or legal offices can call the counsellors rather than leaving the survivor alone.
flags: First-centre language must not become triumphalist; donor technical-support source base; current capacity and local evaluation needed.
evidence: Pacific Data Hub TICC launch page; Pacific Women Lead North Pacific counselling page; TICC/Eleanor IWD2022 page.

name: Women United Together Marshall Islands (WUTMI) / Weto In Mour
location: Republic of the Marshall Islands; Majuro and Ebeye public line
office: Weto In Mour “Place of Life” counselling and support service for women and girl survivors
status: KEEP; NORTH-PACIFIC FIRST-COUNSELLING-SERVICE LINE; OUTER-ISLAND-ACCESS AND DONOR-FUNDING FLAGS
work: WUTMI operates Weto In Mour, RMI’s first counselling/support service for women and girl survivors of GBV, with Majuro and Ebeye service lines and prevention/awareness work.
why: The office tries to make a place-of-life reachable in an atoll state where “come to the centre” may already be an impossible instruction.
flags: Do not expose survivor stories or operational details; funding/current capacity needs refresh; keep support and prevention distinct.
evidence: Pacific Data Hub WUTMI record; WUTMI Ebeye launch PDF; Pacific Women Lead North Pacific counselling page.

name: FatuLei / Tuvalu Women for Change Association and Tuvalu GBV counsellor-training pool
office: Counsellor-pool where service infrastructure is still thin / training-to-door threshold
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP; CAPACITY-BUILDING NOT EQUIVALENT TO SERVICE-CAPACITY; TUVALU GAP ENTRY
work: FatuLei participated in and supported FWCC-facilitated GBV counsellor training in Funafuti for 34 cross-sector community advocates from police, judiciary, community, church, Social Welfare, youth, and FatuLei.
why: This is the office before the office: a survivor-centred door being built through trained people spread across scarce systems.
flags: Training is not a 24/7 service, crisis centre, safe house, transport route, or complaint mechanism; direct FatuLei and Tuvalu service data still needed.
evidence: FWCC Tuvalu training start and completion pages; Tuvalu CEDAW report page.

name: LifeLine Port Moresby / Lifeline PNG counselling and refuge line
office: Counselling plus crisis accommodation for women experiencing violence / emotional-support threshold
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP; CURRENT-STATUS-CHECK REQUIRED; PNG SURVIVOR-CARE AND CRISIS-COUNSELLING ADJACENT LINE
work: LifeLine International describes LifeLine Port Moresby as offering telephone and face-to-face counselling, a refuge, drop-in counselling, crisis accommodation, case management, and repatriation services; Australian High Commission material corroborates a Lifeline-run refuge and counselling/referral services.
why: Counselling, safe accommodation, case management, and repatriation meet where danger is immediate and options are fragmented.
flags: Verify current operating status before referral; do not list as live emergency directory; no refuge location details; distinguish from 1-Tok/Femili/Bel Isi entry.
evidence: LifeLine International PNG member page; Australian High Commission PNG Lifeline refuge renovation page.

name: Regional GBV Counselling Framework / RWG and Pacific Women’s Network to End Violence Against Women
location: Pacific regional framework; launch in Suva, Fiji
office: Minimum standards for safe, ethical, survivor-centred GBV counselling across Pacific countries
status: OFFICE-CANON / FRAMEWORK-CANDIDATE; REGIONAL-STANDARDS-BACKBONE; IMPLEMENTATION-GAP FLAG
work: Regional framework launched in February 2026 by the Regional Working Group and Pacific Women’s Network to strengthen GBV counselling standards; includes minimum standards for ethical, safe, survivor-centred practice, confidentiality, safeguarding, conduct, and accountability.
why: The framework is the underlay of the door: a shared minimum grammar for the person who receives disclosure and must not harm the survivor again.
flags: A framework is not implementation; requires country-by-country adoption, funding, supervision, and accountability checks.
evidence: PINA/SPC framework launch report; Pacific Women Lead 2024–25 progress-report page.

name: Palau Family Protection Act Working Group / inter-ministerial GBV first-response line
location: Republic of Palau; Koror / national first-response system
office: Law-to-door GBV response: health, police, justice, statistics, and case-evidence integrity
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP; LAW-TO-DOOR IMPLEMENTATION ENTRY; HEALTH-FIRST-RESPONDER AND EVIDENCE-CHAIN FLAGS
work: Inter-ministerial Family Protection Act implementation MoU, health-sector GBV training for clinicians/nurses/case managers, data/evidence support for front-line workers, and whole-of-nation first-response coordination.
why: The survivor threshold is an emergency room, police intake, case file, evidence chain, or ministry handoff that does not lose the person to silence or poor coordination.
flags: Law/MoU/training not equal service; confidentiality and consent; data not surveillance; cultural/religious leader precondition risk.
evidence: UNFPA / Spotlight 2023 Palau GBV response article; UNDP Justice Pathways report page.

name: Nauru Domestic Violence and Family Protection Act / Family Protection Coordination Committee / safety-order threshold
location: Republic of Nauru; national court, police, WASDA / service-provider line
office: Protection-order and safety-order door under scarce services
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP; LAW-TO-DOOR IMPLEMENTATION ENTRY; RECONCILIATION / COMPULSORY-COUNSELLING CAUTION
work: DVFPA 2017, Family Protection Coordination Committee, police safety orders, court protection orders, service-provider training and referral mapping including Child Protection, Women’s Affairs, Safe House, DV Unit, Education, and Health.
why: The office is the survivor being able to ask for protection and be connected to support without being pushed back into danger.
flags: Compulsory counselling / family repair language is a red flag; protection orders need enforcement; do not infer current safe-house capacity.
evidence: Nauru Judiciary domestic/family violence page; DFAT Nauru DVFPA implementation article; Pacific Data Hub Nauru EVAW collection.

name: Nauru counselling and social-work qualification pool / service-capacity precursor
office: Counselling and social-work capacity where formal survivor services are thin
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP; CAPACITY-BUILDING ENTRY; NOT SERVICE-CAPACITY
work: Pacific Community Health and Wellbeing Education project supporting five women and one man undertaking Diploma-level community health and wellbeing / counselling-social-work capacity.
why: The law is too thin without trained people who can receive disclosure, manage risk, and refer safely.
flags: Diploma/training not live service; current employment/supervision/caseload/privacy unknown; no heroing trainees.
evidence: Pacific Data Hub Nauru counselling qualifications entry and Nauru EVAW collection.

name: FSM Pohnpei / Kosrae Family Protection Adviser
location: Federated States of Micronesia; Pohnpei and Kosrae implementation line
office: Family-protection-law implementation adviser / service collaboration and gap repair
status: PROVISIONAL KEEP; LAW-TO-DOOR IMPLEMENTATION ENTRY; ADVISER-NOT-SERVICE WARNING
work: Adviser working with FSM Department of Health and Social Affairs to support Pohnpei Domestic Violence Act 2017 and Kosrae Family Protection Act 2014 implementation, strengthening services and collaboration.
why: The connective work asks whether Pohnpei/Kosrae law produces coordinated survivor support.
flags: Adviser not service; current refresh needed; collaboration must protect survivor consent and confidentiality.
evidence: Pacific Data Hub Family Protection Adviser entry; FSM EVAW Pohnpei/Chuuk mapping entry.

name: Pohnpei Division of FSM Department of Health and Social Affairs — first GESI/GBV staff workshop
location: Pohnpei State, Federated States of Micronesia
office: Government-staff orientation as pre-referral door for GBV survivors
status: SCOUT / PROVISIONAL KEEP; CAPACITY-BUILDING ENTRY; NOT CRISIS-CENTRE CAPACITY
work: First Gender Equality and GBV staff workshop for new Pohnpei DHSA staff around GESI, GBV, intersectionality, and everyday government work.
why: The survivor’s first government contact may be non-specialist staff; the threshold is whether they know enough not to blame, expose, dismiss, or misroute.
flags: Training not specialist service; confidentiality and consent; current practice unknown.
evidence: Pacific Data Hub Pohnpei DHSA training entry; Pacific Women Lead North Pacific counselling article.

name: Niue GBV service-gap marker / family-tree mapping intervention
office: Negative-space office: no/limited formal survivor-service door; family-space disclosure/accountability research
status: GAP-MARKER; PROVISIONAL KEEP AS NEGATIVE-SPACE ENTRY; NOT A SERVICE DIRECTORY
work: Pacific counselling review reported Niue had no counselling services for survivors of violence; 2021 family-tree mapping article examines privacy-conscious family-space dynamics around disclosure, accountability, education and talanoa/gossip.
why: The cube records absence honestly rather than inventing an office; research can name hidden dynamics but is not crisis service.
flags: Research not service; small-community privacy risk; family interventions can trap or help; no live referral claim.
evidence: Pacific Data Hub Review of Counselling Services in the Pacific; Pacific Health Dialog family-tree mapping article.

name: Regional Working Group on the Implementation of Family Protection / Domestic Violence Legislation (RWG)
location: Pacific regional; 6th annual meeting held in Aiwo, Nauru
office: Regional law-to-practice backbone for domestic-violence / family-protection legislation
status: OFFICE-CANON / FRAMEWORK-CANDIDATE; LAW-TO-DOOR BACKBONE; RESOURCE-GAP AND DATA-SYSTEM FLAGS
work: Regional forum tracking FP/DV legislation implementation, technical assistance, data systems, resourcing, subcommittees, and counselling-framework launch commitments.
why: The RWG is the hinge asking whether law becomes practice across Pacific family-protection/domestic-violence systems.
flags: Regional framework not local access; data systems privacy; partnership precondition risks; resources not implementation.
evidence: RWG 6th Annual Meeting outcomes document; Pacific Women Lead RWG/counselling-framework report.

name: UNDP / Micronesian Legal Services Corporation — Justice Pathways report for FSM, Palau, and RMI
location: FSM; Palau; Republic of the Marshall Islands; Pacific regional legal-capacity line
office: Legal-capacity review as a map between violence, law, and survivor justice
status: FRAMEWORK-CANDIDATE; JUSTICE-ACCESS MAP; NOT LEGAL ADVICE / NOT SERVICE CAPACITY
work: June 2025 UNDP publication reviewing legislation and broader legal capacities to respond to violence against women and children across Palau, RMI, and FSM.
why: A legal-capacity map helps the cube keep law, remedy, culture, service access, and survivor safety distinct.
flags: Not legal advice; not service; cross-country report can smooth local differences; pathways require local counsel/support.
evidence: UNDP Justice Pathways publication page and PDF.
